newsitem.title: INDIA: India's BSE shifts 22 stocks to the "A" category.
newsitem.headline: India's BSE shifts 22 stocks to the "A" category.

text.p: India's Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) has upgraded the shares of 22 of the country's firms to its "A" category of scrips in a bid to boost liquidity on the bourse, an official said on Sunday.

Among the firms whose shares have been upgraded are Atlas Copco (India) Ltd, BPL Ltd, Burroughs Wellcome India Ltd, Dabur India Ltd, Exide Industries Ltd, Finolex Cables Ltd, German Remedies Ltd, Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilisers Ltd, Hotel Leela Venture Ltd, MRF Ltd, Parke Davis (India) Ltd, Pfizer Ltd, Ponds India Ltd, Procter and Gamble India Ltd, Reliance Capital Ltd, and Sesa Goa Ltd.
Also included are SKF Bearings Ltd, Smithkline Beecham Pharmaceuticals Ltd, Supreme Industries Ltd, Tamil Nadu Petro Products, Voltas Ltd and Wartsila Diesel India Ltd.
The shares were selected for upgradation on the basis of criteria like market capitalisation, liquidity and frequency of trading, the BSE official said.
